flags.reason: This exposure is airborne acoustic playback of ultrasonic vocalisations/tone (a 'hypersonic effect' study), not a focused/transcranial ultrasound device aimed at the brain; the target and device classification is approximate and the pressure/intensity domain framework does not clearly apply.

No group sizes or total are stated in the main text; ANOVA degrees of freedom (F(2,19)) imply a total of 22 animals across three groups for the EPM test, but this is not an explicit statement and was not used to fill the field.

'other' refers to the broadband white noise (35-100 kHz) condition used as a frequency-specificity control rather than a classic sham/control-site arm; this does not match any listed sham_type term precisely.

readout_other: Hyperemotionality scoring; elevated plus maze test (latency to open arm, time in open arm); plasma corticosterone assay
direction_notes: Playback of recorded ~50 kHz USVs or artificial 50-kHz ultrasound for 24 h reduced hyperemotionality scores, EPM open-arm-entry latency and plasma corticosterone in olfactory-bulbectomized rats; broadband white noise (35-100 kHz) had no significant effect, suggesting frequency specificity. The study measured behavioural/hormonal outcomes only and did not assess direction of neural excitation or inhibition.

exposures.label: ~50 kHz airborne ultrasound exposure (recorded USVs and artificial tone)

timing.protocol_description: After surgery, rats were placed in a cage in a soundproof box (23 C, 10 Lux) and exposed to high-frequency (~50 kHz) USVs or artificial 50-kHz ultrasound for 24 h, emitted directly into the cage using an UltraSoundGate Player 116; white noise (35-100 kHz) was used as a frequency-specificity control and a no-ultrasound control group was kept in the soundproof box for 24 h.
